original_question: If every unresolved case for partially shattering k-sets with permutations still falls into one of the three known asymptotic regimes, determine for which values of t the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) occurs.
target_in_paper: Section 14, "Partially shattering k-sets with permutations," second bullet following Theorem 14.2: "If not, then for which t does the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) occur?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the paper is asking the conditional follow-up question about the location of the transition between the Theta(log log n) and Theta(log n) regimes for partial shattering with permutations, rather than the broader neighboring question of whether some new asymptotic regime exists at all.
missing_details: You need to define the extremal quantity f_k(n,t): the minimum size of a family P of permutations of [n] that t-shatters every k-subset of [n].
You need to define t-shattering precisely: for every k-subset X of [n], the restrictions of the permutations in P to X must realize at least t distinct orders.
The paper's open transition question is about fixed k > 3; the case k = 3 is already settled.
The unresolved values of t should be stated explicitly: k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!; outside this range the asymptotics were already known in the Johnson-Wickes paper.
The three regimes should be named explicitly as Theta(1), Theta(log log n), and Theta(log n).
The asymptotics are with respect to n -> infinity, with k and t fixed.

If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, you should specify what Theta(log log n) and Theta(log n) mean here: there exist constants c, C, N > 0, depending on k and t, such that the relevant inequalities hold for all n >= N.
The conditional clause should be tied to the immediately preceding open question in the paper: namely, assume there are no t-values whose extremal size lies outside the three known regimes.
The phrase "extremal family" should be unpacked as "a family of minimum possible size f_k(n,t)."
refined_question: For a fixed integer k > 3 and an integer t with k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!, let f_k(n,t) be the minimum size of a family P ⊆ S_n such that, for every k-subset X ⊆ [n], the restrictions of the permutations in P to X realize at least t distinct orders. Assuming that for every such t the asymptotic growth of f_k(n,t) as n -> infinity falls into one of the three known regimes Theta(1), Theta(log log n), or Theta(log n), determine exactly for which values of t one has f_k(n,t) = Theta(log log n) and for which values of t one has f_k(n,t) = Theta(log n); equivalently, locate the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) within the unresolved interval k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!.
justification: The draft is already close to the paper's intended target, but the official question in Section 14 is a conditional follow-up to the preceding question asking whether any fourth regime exists. To make it stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the paper's notation f_k(n,t), the definition of t-shattering, the fact that k > 3 is the unresolved case, and the exact unresolved range k + 1 <= t <= 2(k - 1)!. I have kept the scope on the specific partial-shattering problem for permutations and did not broaden it to Furedi's more general S-mixing framework.
